title: CyclicFullWidthPerceptron.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Strict feasibility in a bilinear parameterization: writing θ=(W,v), each sample must satisfy vᵀWqᵢ>0. These constraints are nonconvex jointly in W and v; no scalar optimization objective is specified.

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Finite-data linear separation represented by a two-layer linear model of width dimension+1, with a prescribed cyclic, mistake-triggered update family.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query selects one sample index and parameter θ and returns its exact margin derivative, represented by direction using Euclidean and Frobenius coordinates. Replies have no noise or history dependence.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The same query returns the exact scalar margin of the selected sample. Every query counts, including those with positive margin that cause no parameter update.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Features lie in ℝᵈ with Euclidean geometry; W is an unrestricted (d+1)×(d+1) linear map and v∈ℝᵈ⁺¹.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details:
Public parameters are d, n=count>0, κ, μ, ν, with 0<κ≤1, 0<μ≤κ⁴/2²⁰, and 0≤ν≤κ¹²μ²/2⁵⁶. Hidden residuals rᵢ and offsets δᵢ satisfy ‖rᵢ‖≤1, 0≤δᵢ≤ν, and ⟨w,rᵢ⟩≥κ for some hidden unit w. Signed samples are q₀=(1,0) and qᵢ₊₁=(-(1+δᵢ),-μrᵢ). Offsets are fixed data, not oracle errors.
Initialization is W=I and v=0. A fixed positive step size updates both layers using the returned direction exactly when the margin is nonpositive. Queries cycle through all n+1 samples, starting at index zero.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The final output must have strictly positive margin on every sample. There is no epsilon tolerance or required positive margin magnitude. The supplied fixed budget is (n+1)⌈256/κ⁴⌉ oracle calls.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CyclicFullWidthPerceptron.lean: Separates, spec.successful, family; supplied extracted budget for OracleTemplate.CyclicFullWidthPerceptronAcceleration.result.

accuracy.label: deterministic
accuracy.details: Separation is required for every outcome ω, including every algorithm and oracle seed, rather than only in expectation or almost surely.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines specially scaled, nearly opposing samples and tightly bounded offsets with a prescribed bilinear initialization and cyclic mistake-triggered updates. These restrictions define a specialized separation problem.

descriptionHtml:
Cyclic Full-Width Perceptron

We consider strict separation by a two-layer linear model with parameters W∈R(d+1)×(d+1) and v∈Rd+1, where d is the feature dimension. Its margin on an input q∈Rd+1 is mq(W,v)=v⊤Wq. The inputs comprise an anchor and perturbed opposite inputs whose residual features have bounded norms and a common positive separating projection. The perturbation scales obey explicit smallness conditions. The oracle returns the exact margin and its parameter gradient. We analyze the cyclic full-width perceptron, initialized at the identity matrix and zero head. The goal is an output with strictly positive margins on every input, for every realization.

Write n≥1 for the number of non-anchor inputs and take d∈Z≥0. The algorithm receives d,n,κ,μ,ν, with 0<κ≤1,0<μ≤κ4220,0≤ν≤κ12μ2256. The instance consists of residual vectors ri∈Rd and offsets δi∈R, for i=1,…,n, accessed through the oracle. They define the inputs q0=(10),qi=(−(1+δi)−μri),i=1,…,n. All vector inner products and norms are Euclidean.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Residual separation and offsets). The data satisfy 0≤δi≤ν,∥ri∥≤1,i=1,…,n. There exists w∈Rd such that ∥w∥=1,⟨w,ri⟩≥κ,i=1,…,n.

To specify the full-width parameterization, write W=(au⊤cM),v=(bh), where a,b∈R, u,c,h∈Rd, and M:Rd→Rd is linear. For q=(s,z)∈R×Rd, the margin is mq(W,v)=b(as+⟨u,z⟩)+⟨h,sc+Mz⟩. A query specifies an index i∈{0,…,n} and parameters (W,v). The oracle returns (mqi(W,v),(vqi⊤,Wqi)). The second component is the parameter gradient, using the Frobenius inner product for matrices and the Euclidean inner product for the head.

Our result is algorithm-specific: we analyze the cyclic full-width perceptron. The method chooses a fixed step size η>0 from the available inputs and initializes W0=Id+1,v0=0,i0=0. At call t≥0, it queries (it,Wt,vt) and sets γt=mqit(Wt,vt),(Wt+1,vt+1)={(Wt+ηvtqit⊤,vt+ηWtqit),γt≤0,(Wt,vt),γt>0,it+1=(it+1)mod(n+1). Both parameter updates use the parameters before the update. The index advances after every query, including queries with positive margin.

After an allotted budget of T∈Z≥0 oracle calls, the output is the last parameter pair (W¯,v¯)=(WT,vT). The required accuracy is strict separation: mqi(W¯,v¯)>0,i=0,…,n, for every realization of any algorithm randomness.

comparisonHtml:
Signed data in Rd+1 are q0=(1,0) and qi=(−(1+νi),−μui), 1≤i≤N, with N≥1, ∥ui∥≤1, and a unit w satisfying ⟨w,ui⟩≥κ. Parameters obey 0<κ≤1, 0<μ≤κ4/220, and 0≤νi≤ν≤κ12μ2/256. The exact per-example oracle returns v⊤Wqi and its parameter gradient. The setup requires cyclic, constant-positive-step mistake updates from W=I,v=0, with the current parameters as output; (1) uses η=κ6/228. The target is deterministic strict separation, v⊤Wqi>0 for every i.

(3) Rescaled linear Perceptron; derived bound (Novikoff 1963) O((N+1)/κ2) calls on (qi,0,qi′/μ), including a certifying pass. Same oracle; outside the required update family. (3) certifies separation without κ and converges on arbitrary separable data.

(5) Noisy quadratic Perceptron (Tyurin 2026), Thm. 5.1 O(DmL1L2[1+log(DmL1L2)]) calls, success probability ≥1−ρ. Two-sample dataset (5), 0<m≤1/10, nonzero initial alignment; prescribed step and noise tuning. (1): Method-specific analysis for many conflicting residual directions, noiseless and deterministic. (5) uses tuned noise on two samples outside the slab; rates are not comparable. (1) analyzes full width, not the size-2 convolution of (5); its slab theorem does not cover (5)’s dataset.

Abbr: N: negative-example count; d: residual dimension; κ: latent margin; μ: residual scale; ν: offset bound; W,v: layer matrix and head; LP: linear program. Costs count individual example queries, including scans. In (5), D,m are that paper’s dimension and margin parameter (distinct from d,μ here), 0<ρ<1 is failure probability, r=∥θ0∥2/|⟨θ0,vm,+⟩|2, vm,+ is its unit eigenvector of eigenvalue m, L1=1+log⁡(r/ρ), and L2=1+log⁡(Dr/m).

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.LinearMap

open OracleTemplate
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.CyclicFullWidthPerceptron

abbrev Features (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

@[ext]
structure Space (d : ℕ) where
  a : ℝ
  row : Features d
  column : Features d
  matrix : Features d →L[ℝ] Features d
  b : ℝ
  head : Features d

abbrev Input (d : ℕ) := ℝ × Features d

noncomputable def linearPart {d : ℕ} (θ : Space d) (q : Input d) : Input d :=
  (θ.a * q.1 + ⟪θ.row, q.2⟫, q.1 • θ.column + θ.matrix q.2)

noncomputable def move {d : ℕ} (θ : Space d) (η : ℝ) (g : Space d) : Space d :=
  ⟨θ.a + η * g.a, θ.row + η • g.row, θ.column + η • g.column,
    θ.matrix + η • g.matrix, θ.b + η * g.b, θ.head + η • g.head⟩

structure Params where
  dimension : ℕ
  count : ℕ
  κ : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  ν : ℝ

structure Data (d n : ℕ) where
  residual : Fin n → Features d
  offset : Fin n → ℝ

noncomputable def sample (p : Params) (D : Data p.dimension p.count) :
    Fin (p.count + 1) → Input p.dimension :=
  Fin.cases (1, 0) (fun i => (-(1 + D.offset i), -p.μ • D.residual i))

noncomputable def margin {d : ℕ} (q : Input d) (θ : Space d) : ℝ :=
  θ.b * (linearPart θ q).1 + ⟪θ.head, (linearPart θ q).2⟫

noncomputable def direction {d : ℕ} (q : Input d) (θ : Space d) : Space d :=
  ⟨θ.b * q.1, θ.b • q.2, q.1 • θ.head, InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℝ θ.head q.2,
    (linearPart θ q).1, (linearPart θ q).2⟩

structure Reply (d : ℕ) where
  value : ℝ
  direction : Space d

noncomputable def answer (p : Params) (D : Data p.dimension p.count)
    (q : Fin (p.count + 1) × Space p.dimension) : Reply p.dimension :=
  ⟨margin (sample p D q.1) q.2, direction (sample p D q.1) q.2⟩

def Geometry (p : Params) (D : Data p.dimension p.count) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, 0 ≤ D.offset i ∧ D.offset i ≤ p.ν) ∧
    (∀ i, ‖D.residual i‖ ≤ 1) ∧
    ∃ w : Features p.dimension, ‖w‖ = 1 ∧ ∀ i, p.κ ≤ ⟪w, D.residual i⟫

def Separates (p : Params) (D : Data p.dimension p.count) (θ : Space p.dimension) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, 0 < margin (sample p D i) θ

noncomputable def initial (d : ℕ) : Space d := ⟨1, 0, 0, ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ _, 0, 0⟩

def family (p : Params)
    (A : Algorithm (Fin (p.count + 1) × Space p.dimension) (Reply p.dimension)
      (Space p.dimension)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (point : A.State → Space p.dimension) (index : A.State → Fin (p.count + 1)) (η : ℝ),
    0 < η ∧
    (∀ seed, point (A.initial seed) = initial p.dimension ∧ index (A.initial seed) = 0) ∧
    (∀ s, A.query s = (0, (index s, point s))) ∧
    (∀ s r, point (A.update s r) =
      if r.value ≤ 0 then move (point s) η r.direction else point s) ∧
    (∀ s r, index (A.update s r) = finRotate (p.count + 1) (index s)) ∧
    (∀ s, A.output s = point s)

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Data p.dimension p.count
  Query p := Fin (p.count + 1) × Space p.dimension
  Reply p := Reply p.dimension
  Output p := Space p.dimension
  publicInput := id
  valid p := 0 < p.count ∧ 0 < p.κ ∧ p.κ ≤ 1 ∧ 0 < p.μ ∧
    p.μ ≤ p.κ ^ 4 / 2 ^ 20 ∧ 0 ≤ p.ν ∧ p.ν ≤ p.κ ^ 12 * p.μ ^ 2 / 2 ^ 56
  admissible p D oracle := Geometry p D ∧
    ∀ history query seed, oracle.answer history query seed = answer p D query.2
  successful p D output _ := ∀ ω, Separates p D (output ω)
  allowedAlgorithm := family

end LongTails.Setups.CyclicFullWidthPerceptron
